decisions.reason: As a close extension of the core pipeline-components business for the same infrastructure customers, it remains a low-cost option to keep available despite limited visible evidence.
This bracket fits existing metalworking capabilities and project-based customer demand, so management would likely continue offering it because the cost of keeping it is small.
Because it builds directly on established fabrication know-how and complements the firm's infrastructure range, the option value of retaining it is still high relative to its holding cost.

The public waste bin uses relevant fabrication and coating skills but sits outside the firm's main pipeline-focused business, and after several years the remaining uncertainty is no longer enough to justify keeping this peripheral option open.

A multi-model waste-bin-with-ashtray line is more complex to maintain and more distant from the core offer, so management would likely redeploy effort to the established infrastructure business unless clear traction has emerged by now.

Outdoor public ashtrays are furthest from the firm's main application focus and, after enough time to test demand, the firm would likely close this non-core option and concentrate resources on more related products.
